public_rationale: The contemporaneous interview supports the premise that training was costly and that OpenAI sought further investment. The funding reports also show why announced investment cannot be treated as unrestricted cash. But neither establishes November liquidity or the consequences of a material funding reduction. Existing multiyear support could provide a cushion. The causal claim therefore remains unsettled, and its unspecified accounting basis independently prevents a decisive financial verdict.
limitations: The interview and financing report are used because the reviewed sources did not provide matching public financial statements.
Later losses or successful fundraising would not alone prove what OpenAI could withstand in November 2023.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that development costs made continued outside funding necessary to sustain OpenAI's operations and development plans at the time of the post.
Cannot afford means a material funding reduction would force substantial disruption or retrenchment; it need not mean immediate bankruptcy.
The assessment concerns November 2023 funding dependence. Later financing and losses cannot alone establish that earlier condition.
No amount, accounting basis, funding reduction or duration is specified.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous records show that development-related cash requirements exceeded internally available resources and committed funding, so a material reduction in further capital would force substantial cuts or threaten operations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous records show sufficient internal cash generation, reserves or secure commitments to absorb a material funding reduction while sustaining the relevant operations and development plans.
